Avocado Cream for Men: A Simple 1-Minute Routine

By Mohammed Nihal, founderPublished 16 October 2026Updated 16 October 20265 min read
Quick answer

Avocado cream works for men just as it does for women. Use a pea-sized amount at night on clean skin, less on oily areas, and wear sunscreen every morning. After shaving, wait 5 to 10 minutes and avoid any cuts or razor burn.

  • Men's skin is often oilier and thicker
  • A pea-sized amount at night is enough
  • Wait 5 to 10 minutes after shaving
  • Daily sunscreen is essential with kojic acid

Yes, avocado cream for men works just as well as it does for women. Skin is skin. Men's skin does tend to be a little thicker and oilier, and shaving adds its own dryness and irritation, so the main difference is how much you use and when.

If you have never used a cream before, this guide keeps it simple: what it does, how to use it in under a minute, and how to fit it around shaving.

Do men really need a face cream?

Most men wash their face with whatever soap is in the bathroom and stop there. Soap, hard water, sun, helmet sweat and shaving all leave skin feeling tight, rough or dull.

A moisturiser helps skin feel comfortable and look healthier. It is not about looking "made up". It is like oiling a bike chain: a small habit that keeps things running smoothly. Our night cream for men guide covers the basics if you are completely new.

Why avocado cream suits men's skin

  • Avocado gives a soft, nourishing feel, useful after shaving or on rough, dry cheeks.
  • Aloe vera has a cool feel that many men like after a shave.
  • Niacinamide (vitamin B3) helps oily skin look more balanced and pores look less obvious.
  • Kojic acid helps reduce the look of dark spots and uneven patches over time, such as marks from sun or old pimples.

All four are in most Mirc Glow avocado creams. For more on each, see our ingredients page.

How to use avocado cream for men: a 1-minute routine

Night (main step)

  1. Wash your face with a mild face wash, not body soap.
  2. Pat dry with a clean towel.
  3. Take a pea-sized amount and dot it on forehead, cheeks, nose and chin.
  4. Spread it in thinly. Use a little less on the nose and forehead if they get oily.
  5. Do not forget the neck, especially if you shave there.

Morning

  1. Splash with water or use a mild face wash.
  2. If skin feels dry, use a rice-grain amount of cream.
  3. Apply sunscreen SPF 30 or higher. Every day. This matters most.

More detail in how to apply night cream.

Using it around shaving

Shaving scrapes off a thin layer of skin along with the hair, which can leave the beard area dry, red or bumpy.

  • Shave at night if you can. Then the cream has all night to settle on fresh skin.
  • Wait 5 to 10 minutes after shaving before applying cream, so any small nicks can settle.
  • Skip broken skin. Do not apply on cuts, razor burn that stings, or open bumps.
  • Use a fresh, sharp blade and shave with the grain to reduce irritation.
  • Do a patch test first on freshly shaved skin, since it can be more reactive.

If you get razor bumps often, try shaving less closely, or every second day, and give your skin a break on weekends. Gentle, regular moisturising helps the beard area feel smoother between shaves.

If you have a beard, apply the cream to the skin under it with your fingertips, focusing on cheeks and any dry patches.

Men's skin types and how much to use

Skin typeNight amountMorning
OilyHalf a pea, thinner on T-zoneSunscreen only
NormalOne peaRice grain, then sunscreen
DryOne pea, extra on cheeksRice grain, then sunscreen
CombinationOne pea, mostly cheeksSunscreen; cream on cheeks if tight

Common mistakes men make

  • Using body soap or detergent-heavy face washes daily.
  • Applying a big scoop of cream. A pea is enough.
  • Skipping sunscreen. Bike rides and outdoor work mean a lot of sun.
  • Using aftershave with strong alcohol right before cream.
  • Giving up after a week. Skin renews roughly every 4 to 6 weeks, so a more even look usually takes 8 to 12 weeks.
  • Keeping the jar in a hot car or bike seat compartment. Store it somewhere cool and close the lid tightly.

Safety notes

Patch test before first use, especially on recently shaved skin. Our creams contain kojic acid, so wear sunscreen every morning. Stop if you notice burning, rash or many new bumps. See a dermatologist for painful or cystic acne, ingrown hairs that get infected, or skin that stays irritated. More in avocado night cream side effects.

Short answers

Can men use avocado cream? Yes. It works for men's skin the same way; just adjust the amount for oily areas.

Can I apply it right after shaving? Wait 5 to 10 minutes and avoid any cuts or stinging razor burn.

Will it make my face look oily? Not if you use a thin layer. Oily skin needs only half a pea-sized amount at night.

Is avocado cream good for a beard? It is meant for the skin under the beard, not the hair. Press it onto the skin with your fingertips.

Do men need sunscreen with it? Yes. Our creams contain kojic acid, and daily sunscreen protects against the look of new dark spots.

This is general skincare information, not medical advice. Patch test any new product, and see a dermatologist if you have a skin condition.
